name: US visa
fullName: US visa photo (DS-160 and Diversity Visa lottery)
covers: DS-160 (F-1 student, B1/B2, H-1B and other visas)
intro: The DS-160 form and the DV lottery entry both ask for a square digital photo, and reject files that are too big or the wrong shape. JPG is the only accepted format.

documents.label: Visa photo
notes: Square JPG between 600 × 600 and 1200 × 1200 pixels, 240 KB or less. PNG and HEIC files are rejected.
Your head should fill 50–69% of the photo's height.
Plain white or off-white background, facing the camera, no glasses.
For the DV lottery, use a new photo every year. Reusing last year's photo disqualifies the entry.

source.label: Summary of US Department of State digital photo requirements (photo-requirements site; confirm on travel.state.gov)

faqs.q: What size is a US visa photo for the DS-160?
faqs.a: A square JPG between 600 × 600 and 1200 × 1200 pixels, no larger than 240 KB. This tool makes a 1200 × 1200 photo and keeps it under the limit.

faqs.q: Can I upload a PNG or iPhone HEIC photo to the DS-160?
faqs.a: No, only JPG is accepted. Choose your PNG or HEIC photo here and it is saved as a JPG automatically.

faqs.q: Is the DV lottery photo the same as the DS-160 photo?
faqs.a: The digital size rules are the same, but the DV lottery checks photos strictly and disqualifies entries that reuse an earlier year's photo.
